claim: Humans who see a base and target story judge a fact inside a shared causal system as more central to the analogy, and predict it more, than an equally plausible isolated fact. Control readers of the target alone show no such bias. One lab, Illinois; N=48 (Exp 1 and 3) and N=32 (Exp 2).
schema_part: O (mapping choice) / G (check mapping on causal links)
agent_test: Give the agent two candidate matches, one tied to a shared cause chain and one isolated; check whether a prompt asking for the connected one picks it more often than plain prompting, same tokens.

claim: The pull is weaker from memory and not uniform: in Exp 3 (base hidden) the gap shrank to .92 vs .13 predictions and one passage showed no difference. Systematicity is a strong bias, not a law.
agent_test: Run the selection test with the base text removed after a summary step; see if the connected-system pick survives a lossy summary.

claim: Soundness ratings of a match follow shared relational (higher-order) structure and not shared objects: analogy 4.40 vs surface 2.80 vs first-order-only 2.74 (N=30); adding object matches did not raise soundness. Humans in the LLM story test also pick the causal-structure story (N=54), using the same materials.
agent_test: Ask the agent to rate soundness of near-surface vs structure-only matches; compare with the human ordering.

claim: Retrieval and soundness come apart: surface matches are recalled most (.78) but rated least sound; analogy matches are recalled less (.44). Cueing by relations fails at access, not encoding (55% vs 82% forced choice).
agent_test: Test retrieval of stored cases keyed by surface text vs by a relational summary; measure hit rate of the structure-matched case.

claim: Systematicity helped only 8-10 year olds and only in the hardest cross-mapped condition; 4-6 year olds did not benefit and everyone was near ceiling on the easy mapping. The effect depends on how hard the mapping is.
agent_test: Apply a systematicity prompt only when objects are cross-mapped or ambiguous; test whether it helps there and wastes tokens on easy mappings.

claim: Under very short deadlines (about 700-1000 ms) people lean on local matches; relational preference appears with more time. Seen through a review only.
agent_test: Compare local-match vs connected-system mapping at small vs large thinking budgets.

claim: The Lee and Holyoak dissociation is a stable data pattern: removing a shared preventive cause lowers similarity but raises inferential strength (N=42 and N=60). Gentner-lab replication reproduced it (N=70).
agent_test: Give the agent matched and mismatched causal sets; check whether its similarity and inference confidence diverge as in people.

claim: What explains the dissociation is contested. Lee and Holyoak say people build causal models. Colhoun and Gentner say SME mapping plus a later inference step. Myers and Gentner found a carried-over higher-order strength relation (62.28 vs 47.28, N=32), but the similarity effect was not significant (6.25 vs 5.78, p=.13).
agent_test: Implement two variants (pure structural score vs score then causal-model check) at equal tokens; compare accuracy of projected inferences.

claim: SME scores systematicity locally: each matched relation passes 80% of its belief to its argument matches and a mapping scores the sum. Standard solar-system mapping scores 6.03 vs 4.04 and 1.87 for rivals; Karla analogy 22.4 vs surface 16.8. All checks by the same group.
agent_test: Code a small scorer (sum of trickle-down belief over a proposed mapping) as a tool; compare its ranking of candidate mappings to an LLM judge.

claim: Trickle-down scoring works over a wide parameter region (343 points, 6,174 evaluations) but fails to prefer analogies when memory descriptions are bottom-heavy (more surface than relations); order-scaling fails earlier.
agent_test: Test the scorer when case text is mostly surface detail; see whether surface swamps structure and whether re-representation first fixes it.

claim: LLMs do near analogies about as well as people but fail far analogies that need system mapping when surface features mislead: ARN far analogies 39.6% (models) vs 94.1% (humans); GPT-4 far-near 29.1%, far-far 57.1%. GPT-3 was not above chance on far story analogies (p=.065); GPT-4 was.
agent_test: Run ARN-like far items with and without a structure-extraction step; report accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: GPT-4 on the 18 far story analogies is 0.86 (31/36) overall but order-biased (1.0 first, 0.72 second) and falls when the correct story is paraphrased; humans show no order bias (0.78 both orders). Webb et al. had 0.75 for GPT-4.
agent_test: Always run both answer orders and paraphrase variants; treat disagreement as a failure flag.

claim: Whether LLM analogy is robust is contested. Counterfactual letter-strings drop models (human 0.753 vs GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452). Webb et al. reply that failure is counting: GPT-4 with code matched humans (P=0.496). Hodel and West raise memorisation. Only partly resolved.
agent_test: Give the agent a code tool for counting-like steps; compare permuted-alphabet accuracy with and without it.

claim: LLMs lack re-representation: best models reach human level on new feature-mapping tasks but depend on example order and fail the permuted-pairs control (coef -1.7 to -2.3) while humans do not.
agent_test: Add an explicit re-representation step before mapping; test on permuted-pair controls.

claim: Solved chain-of-thought demonstrations that first extract each narrative's high-level message raise far-analogy accuracy by up to 30 points but hurt near analogies.
agent_test: Add a state-the-high-level-message step only for far cases; test on near and far items for the cost.

claim: Self-generated analogical prompting helps only strong models and adds modest gains: GSM8K 75.0 to 77.8, MATH 33.0 to 37.3 (GPT-3.5-turbo); small models gain nothing. No structure-mapping score is used.
agent_test: Equal-token test: self-generated analogies vs the same tokens spent on extra samples.

claim: Text-to-mapping pipelines can recover systematic mappings: top-3 precision 0.87 (ProPara) and 0.94 (psychology stories); question-form relations beat verb-only 0.82 vs 0.48. Yet LLMs are weak at story analogy identification (best about 37.7% vs humans 85.7%).
agent_test: Compare LLM-direct mapping with extract-relations-then-score-mapping.

claim: Many LLM analogy successes are reachable by association: embedding similarity alone gets 77.9% on near analogies; GPT-4 solved over 70% of children's verbal analogies from the C term only.
agent_test: Run an ablation that hides the A:B pair; if accuracy stays, the item does not test mapping.

claim: On ConceptARC, GPT-4 falls short of humans at abstraction (minimal tasks 0.69 vs 0.95; multimodal 0.25). A pointer to abstraction, not directly systematicity.
agent_test: Run a ConceptARC subset with and without the schema at equal tokens.

claim: Comparison is asymmetric: the more systematic item serves as base because more can be projected; this predicts which direction candidate inferences should flow. Bowdle and Gentner 1997: forward comparisons .76 (N=48) and forward inferences .80 (N=48), projected inferences .81 vs .24 in the reverse direction.
agent_test: Let the agent choose base vs target by richness of relational structure; compare with random assignment.

claim: No study shows a connected-structure mapping score beating a plain LLM judge at equal tokens. The nearest, YARN (8B models), found the mapping scorer only competitive on far items after abstraction (Llama 0.46 vs 0.42; Qwen 0.47 vs 0.52 zero-shot), worse on near items, and below the 0.5 random line on far-near cases.
agent_test: Run far-near items with surface lures: plain judge vs extract-abstract-map-score, same token budget, strong model.

claim: LLM judges matching analogies are high recall and low precision when surface cues mislead: GPT-4 precision about 0.50 with a hint, 0.00 without; humans precision 0.67-1.00 but recall 0.06-0.39 (humans n=199, GPT-4 n=60 runs).
agent_test: Add a precision-oriented check that the causal chain lines up before accepting a retrieved analogy.

claim: Longer, more surface-rich stories hurt LLMs far more than people. GPT-4 falls from 89.1% to 60.7% (1 to 30 sentences) while humans stay 72-73%; retrieval from a 200-story bank is near random for long stories (recall@3 3.9% vs random 1.6%).
agent_test: Compress each case to relations before comparing or retrieving; compare against raw text.

claim: Indexing stored cases by a relational summary beats surface text retrieval. Purpose/mechanism vectors: precision 0.739 vs TF-IDF 0.63 at top 1%, and good-idea rate 0.71 vs 0.28 (N=38 workers). A surface embedding retriever was barely above a random trace (38.5 vs 37.6) for math reasoning transfer.
agent_test: Store each case with a one-line purpose and mechanism; retrieve by that line vs raw text; score downstream task.

claim: The abstraction level used for re-representation must match surface overlap: low level helps near pairs, high level without modifiers helps far-near pairs, and no level works everywhere. Raw-phrase mapping scored below chance (MCQ 0.17).
agent_test: Run two abstraction levels and keep the one where the top two mappings differ most.

claim: Frontier 2025-26 models still trail undergraduates on far analogies (ARCANA: best model 48-51% with 12 attempts vs 59-69% for humans on one attempt), with large model-to-model differences (pulley: 100% vs 0% analogy correctness). No ARN retest on reasoning models was found.
schema_part: G (do not trust a single model judgment)
agent_test: Rerun ARN far-near with the agent's own model, with and without extended thinking.

claim: No independent replication of Clement and Gentner 1991, no LLM test of the Lee and Holyoak dissociation, and no token-cost comparison of a mapping-score step against best-of-N were found. Searches were limited by rate limits.
agent_test: Treat as open; build own tests.
